text:
sara (eng-runtime): Heads up — P1 from AcmeCorp. Dedicated pool us-east-2 dropped throughput ~60% starting ~03:10 UTC. Tail latency spiked from 120ms -> 900ms. No obvious GPU saturation. Customers seeing timeouts and some 429s.

mike (oncall): Copy. Any recent rollouts or config flips in that pool?

sara (eng-runtime): deploy-bot reported a config rollout at 02:58 UTC for the scheduler flags (enable_prefer_latency=true). Not a model push. I pulled the last 10m of batcher metrics: average microbatch size collapsed to 1-2 tokens for a lot of requests.

harpreet (eng-runtime): That sounds like continuous-batcher fragmentation. If prefer_latency was toggled, it can shrink max batch tokens effectively and drain faster, causing more small microbatches and queue churn. Can you paste scheduler config?

sara (eng-runtime): Here is the canary config that rolled:

```
scheduler:
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
  continuous_batch_window_ms: 50
  prefer_latency: true
  fair_share: true
```

Kept max_batch_tokens the same but window is 50ms.

nora (support): Customer reported "large drop in throughput" and some requests returning 500 after long queues. They said it started shortly after a config deploy.

kevin (infra): Looking at node metrics: GPU util averaged 35%, CPU & NVLink normal. Queue depth on the batcher spiked with many tiny batches (histogram shows lots of size=1 microbatches). That aligns with fragmentation not noisy GPU.

harpreet (eng-runtime): Sounds like the scheduler is favoring low latency so it flushes early, preventing effective batching for this workload (many medium-length prompts). continuous_window_ms=50ms is too aggressive for this traffic mix. Also check tenant-level shaping — any noisy tenant pushing many short requests?

kevin (infra): Found a tenant (tenant-acme-chatbot) with bursty short-chat traffic starting at 03:05 UTC, coincides. They have many small messages causing the scheduler to flush frequently.

autoscale-bot: [ALERT] Dedicated pool us-east-2 autoscaler scaled 2 -> 4 at 03:18 UTC due to queue length. Throughput did not recover.

mike (oncall): Autoscaling didn't help because per-GPU throughput dropped due to inefficient microbatching. Short-term mitigation: increase continuous_batch_window_ms and raise max_batch_tokens to allow larger microbatches. Consider soft-excluding the noisy tenant.

harpreet (eng-runtime): Agreed. Proposed immediate canary change on one node:

- set continuous_batch_window_ms: 200
- set max_batch_tokens: 8192
- prefer_latency: false (for canary)

sara (eng-runtime): I'll apply the canary to one worker in pool + route 10% of traffic for 5m. Repro steps if you want to test locally:

1) run a short burst of requests simulating many short chats (50 concurrent, mean len 32 tokens).
2) curl pattern:
```
for i in {1..200}; do \
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST \
    -d '{"input":"hi there","max_output_tokens":256}' \
    https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate &\
done; wait
```

harpreet (eng-runtime): After patch, watch these metrics: microbatch_size.avg, batch_window_ms.p95, tokens_per_second, tail_latency. If microbatch_size goes up and tokens/s recovers, we confirm scheduler tuning was root cause.

nora (support): I'll tell AcmeCorp we're investigating and will update within 15 minutes. Marking P1.

deploy-bot: Rollout: scheduler-config v2026.03.15 -> canary on worker-id w-us-east-2-17 at 03:42:05 UTC.

sara (eng-runtime): Canary applied. Initial signs: microbatch_size.avg increased from ~1.6 -> ~9. tokens/s up ~45% on that worker. Tail latency down ~30%.

kevin (infra): Noisy tenant identified. We can either rate-limit that tenant or put them on a separate pool while they optimize. Recommend soft isolation until they adjust client behavior.

mike (oncall): Good rapid results. Next steps: 1) expand config to rest of pool if canary holds for 10m, 2) offer tenant isolation to AcmeCorp or implement tenant-level backpressure, 3) add a regression test that simulates mixed short/medium chat to catch this config flip.

harpreet (eng-runtime): I'll open a quick PR for the regression harness and add telemetry alerts when microbatch_size.p50 drops below threshold for >=2min.

sara (eng-runtime): Noted. I'll keep monitoring the pool for 20m and report back.

nora (support): Sent AcmeCorp a note: "We've applied a targeted fix and are monitoring; you should see improvement shortly."

mike (oncall): Thanks all. If the canary fails, we revert and set temp quota on noisy tenant. Otherwise we'll rollout and close the P1.
